sanjay (eng-runtime): Heads-up — I'm assembling the new dashboard that wires runtime + infra signals for the routing layer (per-route p95, p99; kv_cache_hit_rate; tokens/sec; queue_depth). Need to lock down alerting rules and PagerDuty bindings before we flip to production canary. Want low-noise but actionable pages.
emily (eng-platform): Thanks. Can you list which labels we'll have? route_id, model_id, region, tenant_id? We need those to back our per-route p95 queries and to slice by dedicated vs hosted.
sanjay (eng-runtime): route_id, model_variant, region, tenant_id, capacity_tier. We can emit kv_cache_hit_rate and kv_cache_miss_latency as sample_rate metrics.
dave (eng-oncall): Routing for pages: runtime oncall primary, platform backup. But we should probably only page on high burn-rate or sustained p95 spikes, not every transient blip.
olga (eng-sre): Agreed. Propose two-tier alerts: soft (ops-channel, no page) and hard (page primary). Soft triggers for transient 5m spikes; hard triggers for sustained 15m breaches OR burn-rate > X. Also rate-limit pages with a 30m dedupe.
anna (product): From the product side, we need early warning when SLO burn starts trending up (even if still under SLO) — so add a low-priority metric alert (slack-only) for burn_rate > 1.5 for 6h.
emily (eng-platform): Can we put concrete thresholds here? Suggest: p95 latency per-route > 350ms for 5m => soft slack alert. p95 > 500ms for 15m => page. Kv_cache_hit_rate < 75% for 10m => page for critical routes only. Error rate > 0.5% for 5m => soft, > 2% for 10m => page.
olga (eng-sre): Those seem reasonable. For SLO/burn math: we use monthly availability SLO 99.5% (error budget 0.5%). So a burn-rate of 6 over a 1h window => page (because that would exhaust budget quickly). For clarity: burn_rate = observed_error_rate / allowed_error_rate.
sanjay (eng-runtime): I'll post a draft Prometheus rule for the hard page. Feel free to bikeshed.
sanjay (eng-runtime): ```yaml
- alert: RouteHighP95_Hard
  expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, request_duration_seconds{job="runtime"}[15m]) > 0.5
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: critical
    team: runtime
  annotations:
    summary: "{{ $labels.route_id }} p95 > 500ms (15m)"
    runbook: "https://intranet.redwood/ops/runbooks/route-high-p95"
```
emily (eng-platform): Looks good. Add tenant_id and model_variant to the summary so paging contains context. Also attach dashboard URL and last-deployed model hash.
dave (eng-oncall): Pager mapping: critical -> PD service `pd-runtime-critical`, ops-channel -> #runtime-ops. For soft alerts create slack-notify only and tag `severity:warning`. Also set dedupe to 30m and escalation to platform after 20m.
olga (eng-sre): We should avoid per-tenant paging for now. Page only if tenant_id == "platform-critical" OR route_critical == true. Otherwise slack-only.
anna (product): Can we add a small UX change in the Console: on dashboard rows show the alerting state (green/yellow/red) and a quick toggle to mute a route for 1h? That helps customers and oncall.
emily (eng-platform): Yeah, we'll prototype a mute toggle tied to an infra-metadata tag that the alert rule respects (silence via consul key). UX: mute -> creates ephemeral silence with audit log.
sanjay (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) I will land prometheus rules + alertmanager config with the PD bindings (ETA EOD tomorrow). 2) Emily to add alert state + mute toggle in Console (PR by next week). 3) Olga to review dedupe/escalation policy and runbook (ASAP). 4) Dave to confirm PD escalation timing.
dave (eng-oncall): Confirmed. I'll also add a PagerDuty runbook snippet for responders: quick checks (region capacity, recent rollouts, kv cache warmness).
olga (eng-sre): Small CI note: please include a test for alert noise by replaying last 7 days and asserting < 3 pages per route per week on average.
sanjay (eng-runtime): Will do. I'll post the draft rules and a replay script shortly. Ping me for review.
pagerduty-bot: Created incident policy preview: pd-runtime-critical -> responders: runtime-oncall. Link: https://pd.redwood/policies/pd-runtime-critical
emily (eng-platform): Thanks all — if nobody objects I'll merge the initial alert rules tomorrow and tag a canary rollout to a dev cluster only. Let's iterate on thresholds after 48h of canary data. :thumbsup:
